title: Evangelist-driven Toolkit Adoption Sprints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Run a focused sequence of 6 bi-weekly adoption sprints led by DevX evangelists to increase activation and time-to-first-success for new SDK users.

Why this matters:
- We’ve seen signups convert to active usage slowly in the first 7 days. Improving the moment-of-success helps downstream retention and cited by sales as a blocker for the mid-market funnel.
- This project aims to validate lightweight engagement patterns (sample apps, guided code runs, micro-Quickstarts delivered via in-repo demos) that scale without heavy engineering investment.

Scope:
- Produce 6 sprint packages: 3 SDK-focused (Python, Node, Go) and 3 scenario-focused quickstarts (chat integration, embeddings + search, fine-tune-like prompt pipelines). Each package includes a sample app, a single-page Quickstart, a short video (60–90s), and instrumentation for activation metrics.
- Track activation events: repository clone or template instantiate, first successful API call, first token consumed, and first production flag set.
- Evangelist playbook: sprint script, outreach templates (email and community), in-product banners, and a small experiment matrix (A/B channel cadence).

Success metrics (primary):
- +30% 7-day activation rate for cohorts exposed to sprint packages vs control within 8 weeks after rollout.
- Reduce median time-to-first-success from 48h to <18h for participating signups.

Deliverables & milestones:
- Week 0 (Nov 10): Sprint plan approved, assets prioritized, instrumentation schema finalized (events + properties).
- Week 2 (Nov 24): First package (Python chat quickstart) published to docs + example repo.
- Week 4 (Dec 08): Launch Node and Go SDK packages; start first cohort outreach.
- Week 8 (Jan 05): Complete all 6 packages; publish evangelist playbook and run internal retro.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Engineering bandwidth for sample app maintenance is limited. Mitigation: build packages as extremely minimal reference apps with CI smoke tests and label them low-maintenance; add deprecation policy to playbook.
- Risk: Metrics noise from organic marketing. Mitigation: use isolated cohort UTM params and feature flags in the console to gate experiments.

Open decisions:
- Whether to allocate a dedicated engineering rotation for support of experiment bugs (proposed: 1 engineer x 3 sprints).
- Whether to prioritize an interactive in-browser tutorial (higher dev cost) vs short video + copy.

Related artifacts:
- Sprint plan doc: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEVX/pages/Sprint+Adoption+Plan (internal)
- Example repo (Python chat): https://github.com/redwood-inference/devx-python-chat-quickstart/pull/7
- Analytics dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/devx-onboarding/activation-sprints (view restricted)

Next steps:
- Finalize instrumentation events with analytics (owner: Data Eng).
- Confirm rotation engineer for Dec sprint window.
- Create outreach calendar and community post drafts by Nov 20.
